welcome.metaDescription: Stay-in-Touch reminds you who you haven't talked to in a while. Choose how often you want to talk to each person and see who is overdue first.
welcome.headline: Never lose touch with the people who matter
welcome.subline: Choose how often you want to talk to each person. Stay-in-Touch shows you who you are overdue with, so no friendship fades by accident.
welcome.step1Title: Add the people you care about
welcome.step1Text: Create a card for each friend or family member. A name is enough to start.
welcome.step2Text: Every week, every month or every few months. You decide for each person.
welcome.step3Text: People you have not talked to in a while move to the top. Mark a talk with one tap and the timer starts again.
welcome.linkedText: If a friend uses Stay-in-Touch too, link your contacts. A talk marked by either of you counts for both. Your notes stay private.
welcome.privacyNote: No ads. No tracking. Free forever. Read the <link>privacy policy</link>

about.title: About
about.intro1: This app was created as a way to help people (including myself) to stay in touch with the people they care about.
about.intro2: Everyone has had that experience of waking up one day and realizing we haven't talked to that good friend from college in a couple of months. Thankfully, Stay-in-Touch is here to help!
about.howTo1: To begin, log in with your email or your Google account.
about.howTo2: Next, add a contact card for each person in your life you want to stay in touch with.
about.howTo3: All you need to do is enter their names and how often you would like to contact them, and Stay-in-Touch will take care of the rest.
about.howTo4: Add a contact’s email to send them a link request. Once they accept, a talk marked by either of you resets both timers.
about.me1: My name is Ido Mandelman and I am a passionate Fullstack developer.
about.me2: Originally from Israel, I have moved to Berlin with my wife to start a new life in this beautiful city.
about.me3: In my free time I love reading programming, history, and science-fiction books, cooking and learning German.
about.github: This app is completely open source. You can see the full code on <link>GitHub</link>.
about.website: You can see more of my projects on my<link>website</link>.

whatIsApp.question: What is Stay-in-Touch?
whatIsApp.answer: A simple reminder app for the people you care about. Add a contact, choose how often you want to talk, and the app shows who you should reach out to next.

installAndroid.question: How do I install the app on an Android phone?
installAndroid.answer: You do not need an app store. Open Stay-in-Touch in Chrome and add it to your home screen. It then opens like any other app.
installAndroid.step1: Open Stay-in-Touch in Chrome and tap the menu (three dots) at the top right.
installAndroid.step4: Stay-in-Touch is now on your home screen. Tap the icon to open it.

timer.question: What do the colours and the timer on a card mean?
timer.answer: Each card counts down to your next talk, based on how often you want to talk to that person. When the time is up, or when you have never talked, the card turns red. Mark a talk and the timer starts again.

talkHistory.question: How do I record a talk?
talkHistory.answer: Press the talk button on the contact's card after you talked. Open the talk history (the clock icon) to see all past talks. There you can also add a talk you forgot on an earlier date, or delete one you added by mistake.

privacy.question: Who can see my contacts?
privacy.answer: Only you. Your contacts, the names you give them and how often you want to talk stay private. If you link a contact with a friend, the only thing you share is the dates of your talks.

language.question: How do I change the language?
language.answer: Open Settings and choose English or German. You can do this without signing in. The choice is saved in this browser.

inviteLimit.question: Why can I send only {limit} invites per day?
inviteLimit.answer: Each link request sends an email to your friend, who may not have an account yet. The limit stops the app from being used to send spam, and it keeps our emails out of spam folders, so your invites arrive. The limit counts the last 24 hours.

linking.question: How does linking with a friend work?
linking.answer: Open the menu on a contact's card and choose "Link with friend". Enter your friend's email, and the app emails them a request. Your friend accepts it on their Profile page and picks which of their contacts is you, or creates a new one. From then on, when either of you marks a talk, it shows on both cards and both timers reset. Adding or deleting a talk in the history also changes it for both of you. Each contact can be linked with one friend only. You can unlink at any time from the same menu.

ownCadence.question: If we are linked, do we need the same "how often" setting?
ownCadence.answer: No. Each of you keeps your own setting. For example, you can want to talk every 7 days while your friend chooses every 14 days. A talk resets both timers, but each timer counts down with its own number of days.

deleteAccount.question: What happens when I delete my account?
deleteAccount.answer: Everything tied to your account is deleted: your contacts, their talk history, your links and all link requests to or from you. Then the account itself is removed. This cannot be undone. You can delete your account on your Profile page.

deleteWithLinks.question: What happens to my linked friends if I delete my account?
deleteWithLinks.answer: The links end, and your talks are no longer shared. Each friend keeps their own contact for you and the talks already recorded on it. They are not notified that you deleted your account.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This Privacy Policy explains what information Stay-in-Touch handles, how it is used, and the choices you have. By using the app, you agree to the practices described below.
privacy.noTracking: Stay-in-Touch does not track you. The app uses no analytics, no advertising cookies, and no third-party tracking of any kind. Your activity within the app is not monitored, profiled, or measured for any purpose.
privacy.data: The app stores only what you enter yourself: your contacts, how often you want to talk to each one, your notes, the dates you talked, and an optional email for each contact. All accounts share one database, and every record is tied to your account, so other users cannot see your data. When you send link requests, we also log the time of each invite email, only to enforce the daily invite limit. We keep a list of email addresses that asked not to get invite emails.
privacy.auth: You can sign in with Google or with an email and password. Sign-in is handled by Firebase Authentication. We use your name and email only to identify your account and to show them to people you send a link request to. We do not access your Google contacts, email, or any other Google data.
privacy.linking: If you send a link request, we send the person one email with your name and email and a link to accept. They also see your name and email in the app. After they accept, a talk marked on one side is also recorded on the other. Your friend sees only the dates of those talks. Your notes, contact names and talk frequency are never shared.
privacy.nonUsersTitle: If someone sent you a link request
privacy.nonUsers: Your email address is stored because a user entered it to send you a link request. You get one email per request, with no reminders or follow-ups. The request is deleted when the sender cancels it or deletes that contact. Every email has a link to stop all further emails from Stay-in-Touch. If you use it, we keep your address on an opt-out list, only to honour that choice.
privacy.providers: Your data is stored and processed by Firebase (Google), Neon and Vercel, only to run the app. Resend sends the link request emails; it processes the recipient's email address and the sender's name and email. Your data is never sold or rented, and the app will never send you marketing or spam messages.
privacy.control: You can view, edit, or delete your contacts and notes at any time. Deleting a contact also deletes its notes and talk history. You can unlink a contact at any time to stop sharing talks. You can delete your account on your Profile page. This removes your account, contacts, notes, talk history, links, and all link requests to or from you. Talk dates already recorded on a linked friend's contact stay with that friend, and if you opted out of invite emails, that choice is kept.
